task.description: Idiom/scope/decision-record hard gate (WF-02 Step 2d equivalent) on ISS-0396's ELIXIR-DEV implementation and SECURITY-REVIEWER's PASS, with an explicitly independent sign-off requested on persist/8's :event Multi-step reordering.

result.summary:
Read the real diff (git diff origin/main...HEAD on engine.ex, engine/sub_process.ex, engine/task_activation.ex, engine_sub_process_test.exs, docs/anti-patterns.md), the full design doc (iss0396-task-records-multi-sibling-fix.md), and step-03c-security-reviewer.json's PASS. Ran `mix compile --warnings-as-errors` (clean), the targeted 6-file suite (131 passed, matches SECURITY-REVIEWER's count), and -- since this diff touches persist/8, shared by every Engine.create/2 call -- the FULL suite myself twice: an initial run showed 14 failures caused by two full-suite `mix test` invocations racing on the same sandboxed DB (self-inflicted, from my own background-task handling, not a code defect); killed the duplicate and re-ran clean: `Result: 3052/3054 passed (6/6 properties, 3046/3048 tests), 10 excluded. Failed: 2 tests`. Both failures are `test/mix/tasks/letflow_check_toolchain_test.exs` (REQ-165, unrelated commit 0aa95935, predates ISS-0396 entirely) raising `** (ErlangError) Erlang error: :enoent` from `System.cmd("rustc", ["--version"], ...)` -- confirmed `which rustc` returns nothing in this sandbox, i.e. the Rust toolchain genuinely isn't installed here. Pre-existing environment gap, not a regression: neither failing test touches engine.ex/sub_process.ex/task_activation.ex or any Ecto.Multi/InstanceProjection code path this diff changes.

1) INDEPENDENT SIGN-OFF ON persist/8's :event REORDERING (own read, not a rubber stamp): read the real function (engine.ex:939-1109) before and after. OLD ORDER: :instance_projection (M1, inserts :active) -> :token_record -> Multi.merge (build_sub_process_children_multi/6, chains each sibling's own synchronous-completion cascade, including SubProcess.reconcile_parent_projection/5's DIRECT write of instance_projections.status) -> Multi.merge (timer arms) -> TaskActivation.append_multi (:task_records) -> :event (append_instance_started_event) -> :finalize -> audit merge. NEW ORDER: :instance_projection -> :event -> :token_record -> [children merge, timer merge, task_records, :finalize, audit] unchanged relative to each other.
   Independently confirmed EACH of SECURITY-REVIEWER's three supporting facts by direct reading rather than trusting the write-up: (a) append_instance_started_event/8's Multi.run callback is `fn _repo, _changes -> ... end` and every argument it closes over (instance_id, definition, correlation_key, initial_variables, pins, conflicts, attrs, prefix) is a local variable bound in persist/8's own head, before Multi.new/0 is even called -- moving this step's pipe position cannot change what event it appends or what content it captures. (b) Grepped every Multi step between the old and new :event position for a read of `changes.event`: :token_record reads nothing from changes; the sub-process-children merge's own callback (build_sub_process_children_multi/6) closes over `changes` only to fetch `:token_record` (engine.ex:2585 area, `Map.fetch!(changes, :token_record)`, confirmed by reading build_sub_process_children_multi/6/append_start_multi's call chain) -- zero reference to `:event`; the timer merge only reads `changes.token_record`; TaskActivation.append_multi/6 reads only `previous_pending_task_nodes`/`new_instance_state`, no `changes` at all for :event; :finalize reads only `changes.instance_projection`. No step anywhere in persist/8 reads `changes.event`, so reordering it earlier changes nothing downstream. (c) This is a persist/8-wide, unconditional pipe-position change (every Engine.create/2 call goes through it), but its only observable effect is WHEN EventStore.append/2's own active_instance_guard runs relative to any code path that can flip instance_projections.status before old-:finalize -- for every scenario except the newly-reachable synchronous 2+-sibling-join-to-completion cascade this design's own test exercises, nothing writes that status early, so the reorder is a no-op in practice for every pre-existing test (confirmed by the full-suite pass count above, and specifically re-inspected the REQ-059 pinned-versions/AC4 payload tests and engine_test.exs's own 'snapshot written strictly before INSTANCE_STARTED' test at line 359 -- both pass, and neither asserts Multi-internal step order, only final DB state/event payload shape, which is unaffected by which Multi step triggers the same underlying EventStore.append/2 call first).

2) WAS THIS THE RIGHT FIX, OR SHOULD A MORE TARGETED FIX HAVE AVOIDED TOUCHING persist/8 (shared by every Engine.create/2 call)? Formed an independent judgment, not adopted SECURITY-REVIEWER's framing: the real alternative would be to change SubProcess.reconcile_parent_projection/5 itself -- e.g. gate its direct status write behind some 'am I inside an in-progress root create/2 transaction' check, or route it through EventStore.append/2's own active_instance_guard instead of a bare Repo.update. Both alternatives are worse: (a) reconcile_parent_projection/5's direct, ungated write is not itself wrong -- it is the SAME write shape reconcile_projection/5 (engine.ex, ISS-0397's own fixed sibling) already uses for the ordinary case where the parent instance is a pre-existing, already-INSTANCE_STARTED instance from an earlier, separate create/2 call; threading a new 'is this instance's own INSTANCE_STARTED event already durable' condition into that write would require SubProcess to know about Engine's internal transaction/Multi structure, coupling two modules that are currently cleanly layered (SubProcess builds Multi steps, Engine assembles and orders them) -- a worse violation of module boundaries than a pure ordering fix. (b) Routing the status write through EventStore.append/2 would change reconcile_parent_projection/5's behavior/contract for every call site, not just the newly-discovered root-level cascade, a strictly larger blast radius than reordering one step within the one function that already owns step-ordering decisions for its own instance's Multi. (c) The chosen fix is additive-only in effect and, per the design doc's own §4 correctness argument (re-verified independently, sub_process.ex:1070-1111 load_parent_context/2's fresh unlocked reads inside each sibling's own Multi.merge callback), does not change what any step reads, only when a step that reads nothing from `changes` for :event runs relative to steps that write a shared row. This is the general, root-cause-level fix (make M3 unconditionally durable while the row is still :active, rather than special-casing every current and future write path that might flip status early) -- I agree it is the right choice, not merely an acceptable one. VERDICT: independently confirmed safe and correct, not a rubber stamp of SECURITY-REVIEWER's analysis -- own re-reading of the same code led to the same conclusion by tracing every changes-reader myself rather than accepting the count.

3) IDIOM CHECK: task_activation.ex's new `key_disambiguator \\ nil` optional-arg-with-default pattern matches existing Elixir idiom (default arg preserving all pre-existing call sites' behavior byte-for-byte) and follows this codebase's existing convention of tuple-shaped Ecto.Multi keys keyed by an in-scope struct's `.id` (matches the other four sibling-safe keys in the same function -- reconciliation_key, event_key, projection_key, cascade_lookup_key -- all already `{_, parent_token.id}`-or-`{_, parent_instance_id}`-shaped per the design doc's own §2 rationale, re-verified by reading sub_process.ex:960-972 directly). sub_process.ex's SnapshotWriter alias addition and its two new call sites (deserialize_join_counters in load_parent_context/2, serialize_join_counters in reconcile_parent_projection/5) are the exact same codec functions Letflow.Engine's own build_instance_state/3 and reconcile_projection/5 already call (ISS-0397) -- no new codec, no new abstraction, consistent style. engine.ex's persist/8 change is a pure Multi.run relocation with an expanded explanatory comment; no new function, no new abstraction introduced. No GenServer-doing-gen_statem's-job pattern, no supervision change, no singleton/shared-state introduced anywhere in this diff -- N/A for checks 1-2 of the standard four, this diff is pure Ecto.Multi/transaction-ordering and struct-field plumbing, not process-model code.

4) SCOPE CHECK -- independently confirmed each of the three in-family extensions is genuinely necessary (not gratuitous) by tracing what fails without it, not by trusting the anti-patterns.md narrative:
   - Without the join_counters read fix (load_parent_context/2's `join_counters: %{}` hardcode): the regression test's graph has sp1/sp2's parent tokens both landing on 'join' (PARALLEL_GATEWAY) after their respective SUB_PROCESS completions; the split's own join_counters entry was opened during Engine.create/2's OWN initial root-activation hop chain (via engine.ex's build_instance_state/3, already ISS-0397-fixed, so a real cohort exists in the persisted instance_projections row by the time sp1 completes). load_parent_context/2 is the seed-state builder for exactly this cascade; hardcoding `%{}` means Transition.dispatch_parallel_join/4's `with %JoinCounter{} <- Map.get(join_counters, ...)` guard has nothing to match, failing `{:unknown_branch_id, ...}` for the FIRST sibling to reach the join, well before any second-sibling collision is even reached -- traced this directly against dispatch_parallel_join/4 and Map.get semantics; genuinely necessary and correctly minimal (single-field, matches build_instance_state/3's already-shipped analog exactly, no new codec).
   - Without the join_counters write fix (reconcile_parent_projection/5 never persisting join_counters back): sibling 1's own in-memory Transition.transition/3 call correctly computes an updated cohort (branch 1 now received, still :wait on branch 2), but that update never survives past sibling 1's own Multi step. Sibling 2's own later load_parent_context/2 call (a fresh, unlocked Repo.get inside its own Multi.merge callback, confirmed by re-reading sub_process.ex:1070-1111 per the design's own §4 argument) re-reads the STALE, pre-sibling-1 row and never sees branch 1 as received -- the join can never reach 2-of-2 and never fires, leaving the root instance stuck at :active rather than reaching :completed, which is exactly what the regression test's `assert parent_projection.status == :completed` would catch. Genuinely necessary; same attrs-map-addition shape as reconcile_projection/5's own already-shipped fix, no new lock/write-time behavior.
   - The persist/8 reordering: covered in full under (1)/(2) above -- without it, this same regression test's `Engine.create/2` call raises `{:event_append_failed, {:instance_terminated, :completed}}` because reconcile_parent_projection/5's direct status write (needed for the join to work at all, per the point above) flips the row to :completed before the old-position :event step runs, and EventStore.append/2's own active_instance_guard then rejects the root instance's own founding INSTANCE_STARTED event as terminal. Genuinely necessary for the test to pass at all, and the right-shaped fix per (2).
   All three extensions are correctly scoped: no new abstraction, no framework-ahead-of-need machinery, each a minimal same-shape fix mirroring an already-reviewed sibling (ISS-0397's build_instance_state/3 and reconcile_projection/5 for the two join_counters fixes; persist/8's own existing M1/M4 ordering-comment convention for the reordering, now extended to M3). No scope creep found.

5) TYPE-SAFETY GAP CHECK (does not block PASS, filed separately as required): `key_disambiguator :: term() | nil` in task_activation.ex's new @spec is looser than it needs to be -- every real caller passes either nothing (nil) or a TokenRecord.id (an Ecto.UUID.t()/binary), so a wrong-shaped disambiguator (e.g. an atom, a whole struct) would type-check but produce a working-but-semantically-meaningless key rather than a caught error. This is a real, if narrow, instance of 'a class of invalid state only a runtime/property test would catch, representable more precisely with a struct/typespec change' -- filed as an issue below per the ISSUE_QUEUE.md protocol so it becomes claimable work rather than only living in this summary.

6) DECISION-RECORD CONSISTENCY: read lib/letflow/design/iss0397-join-counters-fix.md in full -- it already cites and cross-references ISS-0396 explicitly (§0's own source list references docs/issues/ISS-0396.yaml, confirming the non-overlap claim independently rather than relying on ISSUE-FIXER's summary) and documents the exact same SnapshotWriter codec this diff's two extensions reuse. No contradiction between this diff and ISS-0397's design. Checked REQ-054 (docs/requirements.yaml, SnapshotWriter/instance_state_snapshots, status: done, S3) -- this diff calls SnapshotWriter's already-public serialize_join_counters/1 and deserialize_join_counters/1 exactly as documented, introduces no new snapshot-table behavior, and does not touch instance_state_snapshots at all. No divergence from any docs/migration/decisions/ record found (this diff touches no web-framework, schema-strategy, or other decision-record-governed surface).

Verdict: PASS. Idiomatic, correctly scoped, no supervision/isolation regression (N/A -- no process-model code in this diff), no decision-record conflict. The persist/8 reordering is independently judged correct and the right fix (not merely adequate) -- not a follow-up-issue candidate; it belongs on this branch since it is required for THIS design's own regression test to pass and is a narrow, well-contained ordering fix with a fully traced blast radius of zero for every other Engine.create/2 call shape.
